title: Summarize Written Text: satu kalimat untuk satu teks
title_target: One sentence that carries the whole passage
goal: Menemukan gagasan utama dan dua-tiga gagasan pendukung sebuah teks akademik, lalu merakitnya menjadi SATU kalimat majemuk 30–45 kata yang benar tata bahasanya dan lolos syarat form.
bekal: menemukan topic sentence dan gagasan pendukung, lalu mencoret contoh, angka, dan nama
menyambung tiga gagasan dalam satu kalimat dengan although, because, which, bentuk -ing, atau titik koma
memeriksa sendiri lima kesalahan yang membuat nilai form atau grammar hilang

blocks.text: Summarize Written Text muncul di Part 1, sesudah semua soal Speaking dan tepat sebelum Write Essay. Di layar ada satu teks akademik **sampai 300 kata** dan satu kotak jawaban. Tugasmu: merangkum teks itu dalam **SATU kalimat, 5–75 kata**, dalam **10 menit** untuk tiap teks. Biasanya ada kira-kira 2 soal. Skornya masuk ke **Reading dan Writing** sekaligus, jadi soal sependek ini menyumbang ke dua keterampilan.

Yang diuji ada dua: menemukan inti teks sepanjang ratusan kata (Reading) dan menulis satu kalimat majemuk yang panjang tanpa patah tata bahasanya (Writing). Orang jarang gagal di sini karena tidak paham teksnya; mereka gagal karena menulis dua kalimat, atau satu kalimat yang hanya menyebut topik.

head: Kriteria
Yang dinilai
Yang paling sering menjatuhkan
rows: Content
Apakah kalimatmu memuat gagasan utama teks DAN gagasan pendukung terpentingnya. Sejak 7 Agustus 2025 isi jawaban tipe ini ikut ditinjau penilai manusia.
Hanya menyebut topik (*The passage is about cities*), hanya merangkum paragraf pertama, atau kalimat hafalan yang bisa ditempel ke teks apa pun.
Form
Satu kalimat, 5–75 kata. Lebih dari satu kalimat, kurang dari 5 kata, atau lebih dari 75 kata: nilai form 0.
Titik di tengah jawaban, sehingga yang terbaca dua kalimat.
Grammar
Struktur kalimatnya benar: ada induk kalimat, dan tiap klausa tersambung secara sah.
Comma splice, kalimat panjang yang kehilangan kata kerja utama, *which* yang tidak jelas merujuk ke apa.
Vocabulary
Pilihan kata tepat dan pantas untuk tulisan akademik.
Menyalin frasa panjang mentah-mentah, atau memaksa sinonim sampai maknanya bergeser.

blocks.title: Dua hal teknis yang perlu kamu tahu
items: **Tidak ada tombol kembali.** Begitu menekan *Next*, jawabanmu terkunci dan soalnya tidak bisa dibuka lagi.
**Pantau jumlah kata sebelum menekan Next.** Batasnya lebar (5–75), tapi kalimat yang membengkak melewati 60 kata hampir selalu menyimpan kesalahan grammar.

**Menit 1–3 · Baca seluruh teks sekali dan cari topic sentence.** Biasanya di kalimat pertama atau kedua, dan sering ditegaskan lagi di kalimat terakhir sesudah *therefore* atau *in other words*. Tanyakan: kalau teks ini hanya boleh menyisakan satu kalimat, yang mana?

**Menit 3–4 · Tandai dua atau tiga gagasan pendukung.** Bentuknya hampir selalu sebab, akibat, solusi, atau kontras. Banyak teks punya **belokan** (*however*, *but*, *more careful research has since …*): pandangan lama, lalu pandangan baru. Ringkasan yang baik memuat kedua sisinya.

**Menit 4–5 · Coret contoh, angka, nama, dan daftar.** Semua yang datang sesudah *for example* atau *such as*, tahun, persentase, rincian percobaan. Daftar diganti satu kata payung: *asphalt, concrete and brick* menjadi *hard surfaces*.

**Menit 5–8 · Rakit satu kalimat.** Gagasan utama menjadi induk kalimat, gagasan pendukung ditempelkan dengan penghubung. Pakai kata-katamu sendiri; istilah teknis dari teks (*microfinance*) boleh dipakai apa adanya.

**Menit 8–10 · Periksa lima hal.** Hanya ada satu titik dan letaknya di akhir · huruf besar hanya di awal kalimat dan pada nama · tiap koma diikuti penghubung atau klausa bawahan, bukan kalimat baru · subjek dan kata kerja cocok · jumlah katanya 30–45.

blocks.text: Alat perakit: enam cara menyambung gagasan

head: Alat
Dipakai untuk
Contoh
rows: *although* · *while* di depan
Mengakui satu sisi, lalu menyatakan sisi yang lebih penting. Cocok untuk teks yang punya belokan.
*Although small loans rarely raise incomes, they help families cope with emergencies.*
*because* · *since*
Menempelkan sebab ke gagasan utama.
*Cities are warmer than the countryside because hard surfaces store heat.*
koma + *which*
Menambah akibat atau keterangan. *Which* merujuk ke seluruh klausa di depannya.
*Printing made books cheaper, which encouraged more people to read.*
bentuk *-ing* (partisipial)
Akibat langsung, dengan pelaku yang sama dengan induk kalimat.
*Printing lowered the price of books, making them available to ordinary readers.*
*and* · *but* · *so*
Menyambung dua klausa setara. Pakai sekali saja; tiga *and* berturut-turut terbaca seperti daftar.
*The brain replays recent experiences during sleep, so sleeping after study improves recall.*
titik koma (;)
Menyambung dua klausa yang masing-masing sudah lengkap.
*Cities store heat in hard surfaces; planting trees can reduce the effect.*

blocks.title: Titik koma: sah, tapi hati-hati
items: Titik koma **tidak** memecah kalimat, jadi jawabanmu tetap satu kalimat. Syaratnya: di kiri dan di kanannya harus ada klausa lengkap, dan kata sesudahnya ditulis dengan **huruf kecil**.
Pakai paling banyak satu. Kalau ragu, pilih *although*, *because*, atau *which*: penghubung menunjukkan hubungan logis antargagasan, sedangkan titik koma hanya meletakkannya berdampingan.

blocks.text: **Kenapa 30–45 kata?** Di bawah 20 kata, gagasan utama beserta dua pendukungnya hampir mustahil muat. Di atas 50 kata, kamu mulai memasukkan contoh yang seharusnya dicoret, dan tiap klausa tambahan adalah satu peluang salah grammar lagi. Rentang 30–45 cukup untuk satu induk kalimat dan dua atau tiga sambungan.

head: Kesalahan
Contoh
Akibat dan perbaikannya
rows: Dua kalimat
*Cities are warmer than the countryside. This harms residents' health.*
Form 0. Sambung dengan *, which harms …* atau *and this harms …*.
Comma splice
*Cities are warmer than the countryside, this harms residents' health.*
Dua kalimat lengkap yang hanya dipisah koma: grammar turun. Obatnya sama.
Huruf besar di tengah
*… the countryside, Which harms health* · *…; However, trees help*
Huruf besar menandai awal kalimat baru. Tulis *which* dan *however* dengan huruf kecil.
Tanpa titik di akhir
*… can reduce the effect at low cost*
Kalimat lengkap dibuka huruf besar dan ditutup titik. Ketik titiknya sebelum *Next*.
Menyalin mentah
Kalimat pertama teks disalin utuh.
Isinya hanya separuh teks dan kosakatamu tidak terlihat. Parafrase, lalu tambahkan gagasan pendukung.
Hanya topik
*The text discusses the urban heat island effect in cities.*
Lolos form, tapi content hampir kosong: APA kata teks tentang topik itu?
Pembuka kosong atau opini
*According to the passage, the writer says that …* · *I think …*
Membuang kata tanpa isi, dan opini bukan bagian dari ringkasan. Mulai langsung dari subjek teks.

blocks.title: Text 1 · Urban heat islands
paragraphs: Cities are almost always warmer than the countryside that surrounds them, a phenomenon known as the urban heat island effect. The difference is most noticeable at night, when the centre of a large city can be several degrees warmer than nearby farmland. The main cause is the replacement of vegetation with materials such as asphalt, concrete and brick. These surfaces absorb solar energy throughout the day and release it slowly after sunset, whereas plants cool the air around them by releasing water vapour. Tall buildings add to the problem by trapping heat between them and blocking the wind that would otherwise carry it away, and waste heat from vehicles, factories and air conditioners raises temperatures further.

The consequences are far from trivial. Higher night-time temperatures prevent the human body from recovering after a hot day, which is why death rates among elderly residents rise sharply during heatwaves. Demand for electricity also climbs as more air conditioning is used, and that in turn produces still more waste heat. For this reason, many city governments are now planting street trees, creating parks and requiring pale or planted roofs on new buildings. Such measures cannot remove the effect altogether, but studies in several cities suggest that they can reduce local temperatures by a noticeable margin at relatively low cost.

head: Langkah
Yang dilakukan
Hasil
rows: 1 · Topic sentence
Kalimat pertama mendefinisikan gejalanya dan tidak diikuti belokan. Itulah intinya.
*Cities are warmer than the surrounding countryside.*
2 · Gagasan pendukung
Paragraf 1 menjawab KENAPA, paragraf 2 menjawab LALU APA dan APA YANG DILAKUKAN. Tiga pendukung: sebab, akibat, tanggapan.
Sebab: tumbuhan diganti permukaan penyimpan panas, gedung tinggi menahan panas · Akibat: kesehatan dan kebutuhan listrik · Tanggapan: pohon, taman, atap yang lebih sejuk bisa mengurangi.
3 · Coret
Buang rincian yang hanya memperjelas.
*several degrees* · *asphalt, concrete and brick* · *water vapour* · *elderly residents* · *air conditioning* · *studies in several cities*
4 · Rakit
Induk kalimat + *because* (sebab) + *, which* (akibat) + *although* (tanggapan).
Lihat model di bawah.
5 · Periksa
Satu titik, satu huruf besar, tiga penghubung, tanpa comma splice.
39 kata: aman.

blocks.title: Model ringkasan Teks 1 (39 kata)
items: Cities are warmer than the surrounding countryside because heat-absorbing surfaces and tall buildings have replaced vegetation, which endangers residents' health and raises energy demand, although adding trees, parks and cooler roofs can reduce the effect at relatively low cost.

blocks.text: Perhatikan nasib kata-kata teks: *asphalt, concrete and brick* menjadi *heat-absorbing surfaces*, dan *death rates among elderly residents rise sharply* menjadi *endangers residents' health*. Yang diparafrase adalah daftar dan contohnya.
Tiga teks berikut dipakai untuk tugas menulis di bagian sesudah ini dan untuk latihan. **Kerjakan tugas menulisnya dulu**: Latihan 1 memuat pilihan ringkasan yang membocorkan jawabannya.

blocks.title: Text 2 · The printing press
paragraphs: Before the middle of the fifteenth century, every book in Europe was copied by hand, usually by monks, and a single volume could take months to complete. Books were therefore rare and expensive, and reading was largely confined to the clergy and a small wealthy elite. This changed when Johannes Gutenberg, a goldsmith working in the German city of Mainz, developed a printing press that used movable metal type around 1450. Individual letters could be arranged into a page, inked, pressed onto paper hundreds of times and then rearranged for the next page.

The effects went far beyond convenience. Within fifty years, presses were operating in more than two hundred European towns and had produced millions of volumes, so the price of a book fell dramatically. Cheaper books encouraged more people to learn to read, and printers responded by publishing in the everyday languages people actually spoke rather than only in Latin. Ideas also travelled faster and were harder to suppress: the writings of religious reformers and, later, of early scientists reached thousands of readers before the authorities could react. Scholars in different countries could, for the first time, consult identical copies of the same text and build on one another's work. Many historians therefore regard printing as a precondition for both the Reformation and the Scientific Revolution, rather than merely a technical improvement.

blocks.title: Text 3 · Sleep and memory
paragraphs: Sleep was long assumed to be a passive state in which the brain simply rested. Research over the past three decades has overturned that view, showing that the sleeping brain is busy reorganising what was learned during the day. In a typical experiment, two groups of volunteers memorise a list of word pairs; one group then sleeps for eight hours while the other stays awake for the same period. When both are tested, those who slept usually remember considerably more, even though neither group has practised in the meantime.

The explanation appears to lie in a process called memory consolidation. New memories are initially held in the hippocampus, a structure deep in the brain that acts as a temporary store. During deep sleep, the brain repeatedly replays recent experiences, and this replay is thought to transfer information gradually to the cortex, where it is stored more permanently and linked to existing knowledge.

These findings have practical implications. Students who stay up all night before an examination deprive themselves of exactly the process that would fix the material in memory, and even a short sleep after a period of study has been shown to improve recall. Sleep, in other words, is not time taken away from learning but a necessary part of it.

blocks.title: Text 4 · Microfinance
paragraphs: In the 1970s, the Bangladeshi economist Muhammad Yunus began lending very small sums to poor villagers, most of them women, who had no property to offer as security and were therefore ignored by ordinary banks. The idea, later known as microfinance, spread rapidly. By the early 2000s it had reached tens of millions of borrowers across Asia, Africa and Latin America, and its supporters claimed that small loans would allow the poor to start businesses and work their way out of poverty. In 2006 Yunus and the bank he founded were awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

More careful research has since produced a more modest picture. A series of randomised studies carried out in six countries compared communities that were offered small loans with similar communities that were not. On average, the loans did not produce a significant rise in household income or spending, and the businesses that borrowers started or expanded rarely grew enough to lift a family out of poverty.

This does not mean that microfinance has failed. The same studies found that access to credit gave families more freedom to decide how they earned and spent their money and helped them to cope with emergencies, and there was little evidence of the widespread harm that critics had feared. Most economists now regard microfinance as a useful financial service for poor households rather than a cure for poverty.

sections.title: Tugas menulis dan cara menilai diri

blocks.text: Untuk Teks 2, 3, dan 4: pasang timer **10 menit per teks**, ketik ringkasanmu di komputer, dan jangan melihat model di *Pembahasan* sebelum ketiganya selesai. Instruksi di tes berbunyi: *Read the passage below and summarize it using one sentence. You have 10 minutes to finish this task. Your response will be judged on the quality of your writing and on how well your response presents the key points in the passage.*

blocks.title: Daftar periksa sesudah menulis
items: **Form.** Hitung titiknya: harus tepat satu, di akhir. Hitung katanya: di antara 5 dan 75, idealnya 30–45.

**Content.** Bisakah orang yang belum membaca teksnya tahu dari kalimatmu (a) topiknya, (b) apa kata teks tentang topik itu, dan (c) satu sebab, akibat, atau belokannya? Kalau hanya (a), kamu baru menulis judul.
**Grammar.** Tunjuk subjek dan kata kerja induk kalimatnya, lalu periksa tiap koma. Subjek baru dan kata kerja baru sesudah koma tanpa penghubung berarti comma splice.
**Vocabulary.** Garis bawahi deretan lima kata atau lebih yang persis sama dengan teks. Lebih dari satu deretan berarti kamu menyalin, bukan merangkum.
Bandingkan dengan model. Yang dibandingkan **gagasan mana yang masuk**, bukan kata-katanya.

blocks.text: Untuk tahu skornya, kerjakan tes latihan resmi berskor dari Pearson, atau bawa ringkasanmu ke kelas Private PTE Linguo untuk dikoreksi pengajar.

exercises.prompt: Choose the best one-sentence summary of each text. — Artinya: pilih ringkasan satu kalimat yang paling baik untuk tiap teks.
items: Text 2. (A) Gutenberg, a goldsmith from Mainz, developed a press with movable metal type around 1450, and within fifty years presses were operating in more than two hundred European towns. (B) By making books cheap and plentiful, the printing press spread literacy and let ideas circulate quickly and widely, which is why historians see it as a precondition for major religious and scientific change. (C) The printing press was a technical improvement that made copying more convenient for monks, although it had little effect on who was able to read. (D) The invention of printing destroyed the authority of the Church and ended the use of Latin, which made modern science possible. ____

Text 3. (A) Volunteers who slept for eight hours after memorising word pairs remembered more than those who stayed awake, and the hippocampus is a temporary store deep in the brain. (B) Because the brain rests passively during sleep, students who sleep before an examination feel less tired and therefore perform better than those who stay up all night. (C) Sleep improves memory, so schools should start later in the morning and give students time for a short sleep during the day. (D) Far from being a passive state, sleep is when the brain replays recent experiences and moves new memories into long-term storage, which makes sleeping after study a necessary part of learning. ____

Text 4. (A) Although microfinance was once promoted as a way out of poverty, rigorous studies show that small loans rarely raise incomes but do help households manage money and cope with emergencies, so it is now seen as a useful service rather than a cure. (B) Microfinance, which was pioneered by Muhammad Yunus in Bangladesh and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006, has lifted tens of millions of borrowers in Asia, Africa and Latin America out of poverty. (C) Randomised studies in six countries have shown that microfinance has failed, because borrowers fall into debt, which is exactly the harm that critics had feared. (D) Ordinary banks ignore poor villagers who have no property, so governments should give them grants instead of loans. ____

exercises.prompt: Does each response to Text 1 meet the FORM requirement (one sentence, 5–75 words)? Write YES or NO. — Artinya: apakah tiap jawaban untuk Teks 1 memenuhi syarat FORM (satu kalimat, 5–75 kata)? Tulis YES atau NO. Yang dinilai di sini hanya form, bukan isinya.
items: Cities are warmer than the countryside. This is because concrete and asphalt absorb heat during the day and release it at night. ____
Cities are warmer than their surroundings because hard surfaces store heat; planting trees and cooling roofs can reduce the effect cheaply. ____
Cities trap heat. ____

Cities are almost always warmer than the countryside that surrounds them, especially at night, because vegetation has been replaced with asphalt, concrete and brick, which absorb solar energy during the day and release it slowly after sunset, and because tall buildings trap heat and block the wind, while waste heat from vehicles, factories and air conditioners raises temperatures further, so death rates among elderly residents rise during heatwaves and demand for electricity climbs, which is why many city governments are planting street trees, creating parks and requiring pale or planted roofs. ____
Although trees and cooler roofs cannot remove the urban heat island effect, which is caused mainly by heat-absorbing surfaces and tall buildings, they can lower city temperatures at low cost. ____

exercises.prompt: In each set, ONE sentence is a comma splice (two complete sentences joined only by a comma). Choose it. — Artinya: di tiap kelompok, SATU kalimat adalah comma splice (dua kalimat lengkap yang hanya disambung koma). Pilih kalimat itu.
items: (A) Cities are warmer than the countryside, which increases the demand for electricity. (B) Cities are warmer than the countryside, this increases the demand for electricity. (C) Cities are warmer than the countryside, and this increases the demand for electricity. ____

(A) Printing lowered the price of books, more people therefore learned to read. (B) Printing lowered the price of books, so more people learned to read. (C) Because printing lowered the price of books, more people learned to read. ____

(A) Although the loans rarely raised incomes, they helped families cope with emergencies. (B) The loans rarely raised incomes; however, they helped families cope with emergencies. (C) The loans rarely raised incomes, however they helped families cope with emergencies. ____

exercises.prompt: Kamu sedang merangkum Teks 3 dalam satu kalimat. Tandai tiap informasi: MAIN kalau harus masuk ringkasan, DETAIL kalau dicoret.
items: The sleeping brain actively reorganises what was learned during the day. ____
Two groups of volunteers memorise word pairs, and one group then sleeps for eight hours. ____
The hippocampus is a structure deep in the brain that acts as a temporary store. ____
Sleep is a necessary part of learning rather than time taken away from it. ____

head: No
Jawaban
Alasan & pengecoh
rows: B

B memuat gagasan utama (*a precondition for both the Reformation and the Scientific Revolution*) beserta jalannya: buku murah, melek huruf, gagasan menyebar. A memakai kata-kata teks tetapi hanya rincian paragraf pertama. C bertentangan dengan *the effects went far beyond convenience*. D melebih-lebihkan: teks hanya berkata *rather than only in Latin* dan *harder to suppress*.
D

D memuat belokan teks (*passive state* lalu *has overturned that view*), mekanismenya, dan simpulannya (*a necessary part of it*). A hanya rincian percobaan dan satu definisi. B bertentangan: otak justru *busy*, bukan beristirahat. C masuk akal, tapi teks tidak membahas jam masuk sekolah.
A

A mengikuti tiga langkah teks: harapan awal, temuan *randomised studies*, penilaian akhir (*a useful financial service … rather than a cure for poverty*). B memakai nama, tahun, dan angka dari teks, tapi simpulannya berlawanan dengan paragraf kedua. C bertentangan dengan *This does not mean that microfinance has failed*. D saran yang tidak ada di teks.
NO
Ada titik sesudah *countryside*, lalu kalimat baru *This is because …*. Dua kalimat: form 0, sebagus apa pun isinya.
YES
Titik koma tidak memecah kalimat. Di kiri dan kanannya ada klausa lengkap, kata sesudahnya huruf kecil, panjangnya 21 kata.
NO
Satu kalimat, tapi hanya 3 kata. Batas bawahnya 5 kata.
NO
Memang satu kalimat, tapi panjangnya 91 kata, melewati batas 75. Ini yang terjadi kalau contoh dan daftar tidak dicoret.
YES
Satu kalimat, 30 kata. Dua komanya sah karena mengapit klausa *which*.
although
Konsesi: mengakui kesan (*looks like a passive state*) lalu membaliknya (*in fact busy*). *Despite* harus diikuti kata benda atau bentuk *-ing*, bukan klausa bersubjek.
whereas
Dua hal dibandingkan langsung: permukaan keras menyimpan panas, tumbuhan mendinginkan (*whereas plants cool the air*).
which
*Which* merujuk ke seluruh klausa di depannya dan menjadi subjek *encouraged*.
because
Sebab: diabaikan bank KARENA tidak punya jaminan. *So that* menyatakan tujuan, dan di sini tidak ada tujuan.
despite
Diikuti frasa kata benda (*its early reputation*), bukan klausa. *Although its early reputation …* akan butuh kata kerja.
B
*this increases …* adalah kalimat lengkap baru sesudah koma tanpa penghubung. A memakai *which*, C memakai *and*: keduanya sah.
A
*Therefore* itu kata keterangan, bukan penghubung, jadi tidak bisa menyambung dua kalimat sesudah koma. B memakai *so*, C memakai *because*.
C
Jebakan paling umum: *however* bukan penghubung, jadi sesudah koma ia menghasilkan comma splice. B benar karena memakai titik koma sebelum *however*.
MAIN
Temuan pokok teks (*the sleeping brain is busy reorganising what was learned*).
DETAIL
Rincian percobaan (*in a typical experiment …*). Fungsinya membuktikan, bukan menyatakan gagasan.
DETAIL
Definisi istilah. Ringkasan tidak butuh nama bagian otaknya.
MAIN
Kalimat penutup teks, ditandai *in other words*. Simpulan seperti ini hampir selalu wajib masuk.

blocks.title: Teks 2 · The printing press (40 kata)
items: The printing press that Gutenberg developed in the fifteenth century made books cheap and plentiful, which spread literacy and allowed new ideas to circulate quickly, so many historians regard it as a precondition for the Reformation and the Scientific Revolution.
Kerangkanya: gagasan utama + *, which* (akibat) + *so* (penilaian sejarawan). *Mainz*, *1450*, *two hundred towns*, dan cara kerja mesinnya dicoret.

blocks.title: Teks 3 · Sleep and memory (38 kata)
items: Although sleep was once thought to be a passive state, research shows that the sleeping brain replays recent experiences and transfers new memories into long-term storage, which means that sleeping after study is a necessary part of learning.
Kerangkanya: *although* (pandangan lama) + induk kalimat (temuan baru) + *, which means that* (implikasi).

blocks.title: Teks 4 · Microfinance (41 kata)
items: While microfinance was originally promoted as a route out of poverty, rigorous studies have found that small loans seldom increase household income but help families manage money and emergencies, making it a useful financial service rather than a cure for poverty.

Kerangkanya: *while* (harapan awal) + induk kalimat dengan *but* (dua temuan) + bentuk *-ing* (penilaian akhir). Teks ini punya DUA belokan; ringkasan yang hanya memuat belokan pertama akan berkata microfinance gagal, padahal teksnya tidak.

blocks.title: Yang perlu dicatat
items: Form adalah nilai yang paling mudah diamankan dan paling sering dibuang. Satu titik, di akhir, tanpa huruf besar di tengah selain nama.

Ringkasan yang baik mengikuti **bentuk** teksnya. Teks sebab-akibat dirangkum dengan *because* dan *which*; teks yang berbelok dirangkum dengan *although* atau *while*. Penghubung yang kamu pilih menunjukkan bahwa kamu paham hubungan antargagasannya.
*However*, *therefore*, dan *moreover* bukan penghubung klausa. Di soal satu kalimat, ketiganya hanya aman sesudah titik koma.
